answer_text: World War I was set off immediately by the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary, who was shot in Sarajevo in June 1914 by a Bosnian Serb nationalist, an act that gave Austria-Hungary the pretext to issue a set of harsh demands to Serbia and ultimately declare war on it. However, that single event only escalated into a continent-wide war because of a much deeper set of underlying conditions that had been building for years beforehand.
